idiom_name: Akka Streams Tcp + Framing.delimiter over ByteString (Source/Flow/Sink)
implementation_notes: In Scala the roles become a stream: Tcp(system).bind(host, port) is the receiver's socket, each IncomingConnection is handled with connection.handleWith(flow), and Framing.delimiter(ByteString(...), maximumFrameLength = ..., allowTruncation = ...) turns raw ByteString chunks into whole messages - the reassembly the classic receiver loop would do by hand - while Tcp(system).outgoingConnection(host, port).join(flow) is the forwarder. Serialization comes from the ecosystem (circe, upickle, akka-serialization) rather than the framework, and back-pressure is transparent, which is the main reason to prefer this formulation; a hand-written actor-based pair (Akka IO) remains justified in a codebase already committed to raw actors or a non-Akka stack.
code_sketch:
val connections = Tcp(system).bind("0.0.0.0", 9002)
connections.runForeach { conn =>
  val receiver: Flow[ByteString, ByteString, NotUsed] =
    Framing.delimiter(ByteString("\n"), maximumFrameLength = 65536)
      .map(_.utf8String).map(decode)                 // String -> Message
      .map(msg => ByteString(encodeAck(dispatch(msg))))   // peer method + reply
  conn.handleWith(receiver)
}

// forwarder
Source.single(ByteString(encode(Msg.reserve(7)) + "\n"))
  .via(Tcp(system).outgoingConnection("peer2", 9002)).runWith(Sink.ignore)
pitfalls: maximumFrameLength and allowTruncation are policy: a delimiter that never arrives plus a generous maximum is an unbounded-memory bug.
A decode exception fails the whole stream unless supervision or recover is added, so one malformed message currently kills the connection.
ByteString is immutable and cheap to slice, but .utf8String copies - decode bytes once instead of at every stage of the flow.
